I’m sorry—I don’t have live‑internet access from this environment, so I can’t pull up current or future weather forecasts directly. However, I can point you toward several reliable ways to obtain exactly the information you’re looking for: | Service | How to Use It | What You’ll Get | |---------|---------------|----------------| | **OpenWeatherMap** (`api.openweathermap.org`) | Sign up for a free key → Call `https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/onecall` with parameters:
`lat=37.8651&lon=-119.5383&exclude=minutely,daily,current,alerts&units=metric&appid=`
For daily forecasts add `daily`. For hourly, keep `hourly`. | Hourly temps, wind speeds, precipitation probabilities & amounts for up to 48 h; daily summaries for 7–8 days (extendable with paid plans). | | **NOAA’s National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI)** | Use their “Climate Prediction Center” API or download GHCND/GHCNP datasets.
Example endpoint: `https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/services/search/v1/query?...` | Historical climate normals, long‑term averages – useful for trend context rather than short‑range forecasting. | | **Visual Crossing Weather** (`visualcrossing.com/weather-api`) | Free tier allows ~1000 requests/day. Query:
`https://weather.visualcrossing.com/VisualCrossingWebServices/rest/services/timeline/37.8651,-119.5383/next10d?unitGroup=mph&include=hours%2Cprecipitation&key=&contentType=json` | Full hourly breakdown for temperature, wind speed, precipitation probability & amount over the next 10 days. | | **AccuWeather** | Requires subscription; offers detailed hourly/daily forecasts through its REST API. | Same as above—temperature, wind, rain/snow chance per hour. | ### Quick Example Using Visual Crossing ```bash curl "https://weather.visualcrossing.com/VisualCrossingWebServices/rest/services/timeline/37.8651,-119.5383/next10d?unitGroup=us&include=hours,precipitation&key=YOUR_API_KEY" ``` This JSON response contains an array of dates, each containing an `"hours"` list where each entry has fields such as: * `temp` * `windspeed` * `precipprob` / `precipmm` Feel free to parse those into whatever format suits your application. --- #### If you’d prefer a quick manual check right now: 1. Go to [open-meteo.com](https://open-meteo.com/) * Enter latitude 37.8651, longitude −119.5383. * Select “Hourly” variables: `temperature_2m`, `windspeed_10m`, `rain_probability`. * Set time range to the next 240 hours (~10 days). That gives you a straightforward CSV/JSON output without needing an API key. Let me know which route works best for you—or if there’s anything else I can do!
